P1.evidence: Opened off the application — 'I saw your application. And it stood out to me that you want to make a diabetes your [b*tch]'. Frame was a three-part agenda, not the scripted four-part where-you-are/where-you-want-to-go/what's-in-the-way/what-you-need: 'I would need to get to know you a little bit more and understand, like, what you're trying to fix right now... and if we can actually help you, and if yes, I can walk you through how Trevor is working with people'. Got agreement — 'Cool? Cool.' — and opened with 'So, what's up with your fitness? Tell me more.'

P2.evidence: Strong on the one thing that mattered least here and weak everywhere else. Work was asked properly — 'do you work? ... is it like sedentary most of the time?' — and the foot was probed hard, including the return-to-walking timeline. But age (45), sleep, energy, training frequency, results and diet all arrived because the prospect volunteered them; none were asked. Conditions were asked only as a closed sweep — 'Do you have any other injuries? Any conditions, any limitations in your movement whatsoever?' — with no hereditary question and no follow-up on the diabetes itself. Height and weight never established at all, on a call where the prospect had lost about 85 lb.

P3.evidence: The deep half ran well and the surface half did not. The prospect pre-loaded his three goals unprompted, so P3a/P3b were never asked. The rep bridged properly — 'Would you say that was kind of an awakening for you?' and 'what would that moment be worth to you, man?' — which surfaced the father's death from COVID and the fear of a walker at 60. He then drove impact outward himself: 'you mentioned when we started, it's that you're looking after kids of your sister?... that's also a thing, the cool uncle that you want to be.' The reflect-back was implicit rather than explicit — 'if you're doing this only for aesthetics, usually it's not enough... but you, what you said about the health journey, and this 5k run' — never landing the scripted 'so this isn't really about X, is that right?'

P4.evidence: Phase 4 was not run at any point. Nothing was asked about what he has tried before, what happened, why it did not stick, or what is actually in the way. This is the structural failure of the call: the prospect is currently succeeding on his own — 85 lb down, ten months consistent, a gym, a trainer, machine loads up 4x in eight weeks — so no gap was ever established and the rep had no root cause to sell against. The only usable gap the prospect named he named himself and the rep did not develop it: 'the training is cool at the gym for one day of the week, but it's like for 45 minutes'.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The rep ran the mirror image — an entirely positive future projection, 'six months from now, you can be in way better shape, way better spot... what actually becomes possible for you?' — and never asked what two more years of the current path looks like, whether he would settle for it, or for a line in the sand. With a prospect whose recent past includes an amputation, the cost of inaction was available for free and was left on the table.

P6.evidence: No commitment check before presenting. The rep asserted commitment instead of asking for it — 'I feel very confident. I don't think I could install you more commitment than you already have' — and went straight into the three pillars. The scripted belief question was eventually asked, but forty minutes later and only as part of the spouse rebuttal: 'Before you speak with your spouse, and money aside, do you personally feel that this can get you to your goals?' The 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' question was never asked, and hesitation was met with a deposit demand rather than a return to Phase 5.

P11.evidence: Close attempted, nothing completed. Payment was pushed repeatedly — 'Let's get this 2K now and we'll get you rolling, man', then down to 'let's do it like this, $500 deposit' — and nothing was collected. The Trevor call was used as the reason for the deposit but never scheduled: 'I need to see what next week, what's his availability to get you on a call with him.' The agreement was mentioned in passing — 'get you signed an agreement and everything' — but not sent or signed on the call. Nothing at all about the welcome email, the Skool community link or the onboarding questionnaire.

objection_plays.detail: Most of the play ran. Isolated with 'money aside, do you personally feel that this can get you to your goals?' and followed with 'why do you feel is that?'. Asked what obstacles the spouse might raise. Went further than the script with a live role-play as Radu. Landed the ownership move — 'it's your decision. It's your responsibility, your health, not his.' Tried to bring the spouse onto the call — 'if he's in the room, let's get him here.' Closed with the refundable-deposit bridge exactly as scripted. Two gaps: he never asked 'is there any reason he would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', and having established that the real blocker was money, not the spouse, he kept pressing the spouse frame.

The financial picture was a third built. He got monthly surplus ('after you pay bills, taxes, groceries, how much is left roughly?') and savings ('do you have any, like a savings or checkings account... At least some of it you could move towards that'). He never isolated first, never asked about credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, or investments — and the $600 bank balance only surfaced an hour in, volunteered, after the plan had already been agreed. He also skipped the 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' reframe. Instead of building the picture and then structuring against it, he cut the scope and the price. The manager confirmed the gap in the same-day review: 'Did you open wallet him, Andrew?' / 'Nope, not properly.'

Triggered by 'can I just have a day? Or can I have the weekend and can we like reconvene on Monday?' He ran 'what's coming up?' and a version of thinking-isn't-the-problem — 'if you want to still think about it, but I know deep down that you already made the decision'. He did not run the belief question at this point (it had been used earlier under OB), did not run 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision?', did not run the identity move, and did not run the final 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from 100%'. The play collapsed into a deposit gate.

Triggered by 'would it make more sense to get this started in the week and a half once I'm able to actually move around'. The rep answered logistically rather than with the play — onboarding takes about that long anyway, Trevor needs 24-48 hours to build the programme, and 'you won't start from the get-go with kettlebells'. It worked, and the prospect accepted it, but none of the scripted moves ran and the answer quietly committed the programme to accommodating an active surgical wound.

Fear was visibly present near the end and the rep named it once — 'you seem a little bit worried. What's coming up?' — then let audio problems bury it and returned to the deposit. None of the certainty, bridge, plane or burned-before moves ran. The manager's read on the same recording was that fear is exactly what ended the call.

Clinical-fit gap, the same hole the playbook already records for the Tyron Giuliani call. The prospect is four weeks into skin grafts on a partially amputated foot, strictly non-weight-bearing, and asked directly about the timing of starting. There is no scripted path for establishing medical clearance, so the rep improvised reassurance — 'he will address all that imbalances, all the mobility work that you need to do before you even start with the kettlebells' — and no clinician was mentioned by either party. The script has no move that would have made him ask.

notes: Excellent rapport and a genuinely good Phase 3 wasted by skipping Phases 4, 5 and 6 entirely — the rep never established a gap, never made inaction cost anything, and never got a verbal yes before presenting, so when price landed he had no leverage and cut the offer instead. Coach one thing: run the open wallet before naming any number, so the $600 bank balance surfaces before a $2,000 first payment is agreed rather than an hour after.
